title: `podman run --cap-add` ignored when `io.containers.capabilites` is set
body:
### Issue Description

I honestly do not know if podman behaves correctly, but I was slightly surprised by the behaviour and could not find what the actual correct behaviour must be.

Basically when the LABEL `io.containers.capabilities` is set (e.g. `quay.io/podman/stable:latest`), then starting the container and try to add additional capabilities with `--cap-add SYS_ADMIN` will be silently ignored.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. `podman run --rm -it --pull=always --cap-add SYS_ADMIN quay.io/podman/stable:latest capsh --print | grep sys_admin`

### Describe the results you received

CAP_SYS_ADMIN is not added to the running container, although it is explicitly requested via `--cap-add SYS_ADMIN`

### Describe the results you expected

Comparing the two different results (first one seems wrong, second one correct):
```
$ podman run --rm -it --cap-add SYS_ADMIN quay.io/podman/stable:latest capsh --print | grep sys_admin
Current IAB: !cap_dac_read_search,!cap_linux_immutable,!cap_net_broadcast,!cap_net_admin,!cap_net_raw,!cap_ipc_lock,!cap_ipc_owner,!cap_sys_module,!cap_sys_rawio,!cap_sys_ptrace,!cap_sys_pacct,!cap_sys_admin,!cap_sys_boot,!cap_sys_nice,!cap_sys_resource,!cap_sys_time,!cap_sys_tty_config,!cap_mknod,!cap_lease,!cap_audit_write,!cap_audit_control,!cap_mac_override,!cap_mac_admin,!cap_syslog,!cap_wake_alarm,!cap_block_suspend,!cap_audit_read,!cap_perfmon,!cap_bpf,!cap_checkpoint_restore```
```
vs
```
$ podman run --rm -it --cap-add SYS_ADMIN fedora:45 capsh --print | grep sys_admin
Current: cap_chown,cap_dac_override,cap_fowner,cap_fsetid,cap_kill,cap_setgid,cap_setuid,cap_setpcap,cap_net_bind_service,cap_sys_chroot,cap_sys_admin,cap_setfcap=ep
Bounding set =cap_chown,cap_dac_override,cap_fowner,cap_fsetid,cap_kill,cap_setgid,cap_setuid,cap_setpcap,cap_net_bind_service,cap_sys_chroot,cap_sys_admin,cap_setfcap
```
